title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car in autonomous mode struck and killed a duck in a Austin residential area, despite a human safety operator being present in the vehicle. The system did not slow down or brake, even though a person was monitoring its behavior. It is not established whether the operator could have prevented the collision or what the timing and visibility conditions were.

The incident reveals a gap between what autonomous vehicle systems can perceive and respond to. The vehicle's developers investigated using logged data and simulation, which showed the car made stops at intersections, but this method does not clarify why the system failed to detect or avoid the duck. A human observer in the vehicle also did not intervene. It is not established what detection range the system has for small moving objects or whether it was designed to avoid animals.

The developer's response included restricting the testing area and evaluating technology improvements, but the specific technical failures remain unclear. Whether the system simply did not detect the duck, detected it but did not classify it as an obstacle, or detected it but decided stopping was not required is not established from the reports.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community concern about self-driving car technology. The incident occurred when the vehicle, which had a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck was well-known to residents as it had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant, which intensified neighborhood outrage about the accident.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode during the incident and investigated the event by reviewing vehicle data and replaying the scenario in simulation multiple times. While a resident claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, Avride stated it found no evidence supporting this claim and said the car made complete stops at all relevant intersections. In response, Avride has adjusted its testing area by excluding certain streets around the lake and is now evaluating improvements to the technology to prevent similar situations. Local residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator.
